name: Role-oriented bots
summary: Each folder is a standing agent role with its own memory and outputs. Use when the owner works with agents across many sessions on overlapping concerns.
when_to_use: The owner repeatedly starts chats that need the same standing context.
Work is ongoing (watchdogs, research desks, ops), not one-shot deliverables.
partitioning_rubric: Partition by WHO the worker is and what it is responsible for, not by subject.
Each role folder gets: AGENTS.md (role, conventions, pointers), STATE.md (current status, open questions, next moves), and an outputs/ or docs/ subfolder.
A role folder is a workplace, not a dump: if a file is a finished artifact with no ongoing role, it belongs in a case or archive folder, not a bot.
Cap the number of bot folders at ~6. More than that and the owner has a roster problem, not an organization problem.

folder_template.agents_md_skeleton:
# <Role name>

## Purpose
<one paragraph: what this worker owns>

## Standing instructions
- <conventions every session should follow>

## Canonical files
- STATE.md — current status; update it when work completes
- outputs/ — finished artifacts

## Boundaries
- <what this role should NOT touch>
folder_template.state_md_skeleton:
# STATE — <Role name>

Updated: <date>

## Current status
-

-

-

example.research-desk: long-running research: dossiers in docs/, STATE.md tracks open questions
example.ops-watchdog: cron-fed monitoring: STATE.md holds current rack/incident model
